Member: Riley Novak, Member ID W755986580
Service: Total shoulder replacement, CPT 23472
Notice Date: 2026-08-10

To the Grievance and Appeals Department:

I am writing, with the support of my surgeon, Dr. Okafor, MD, to appeal the denial of prior authorization for total shoulder arthroplasty (CPT 23472). Your notice dated 2026-08-10 stated the reason for denial as follows: "the imaging findings submitted do not support the medical necessity of the requested procedure." I am asking Molina to reverse this determination.

1. A note on the criteria applied to this denial

Before addressing the clinical record, I want to note for the file that the denial notice did not cite a specific medical policy, clinical guideline document, policy number, or edition/version of criteria that was applied to reach this decision. I have searched Molina's publicly posted Molina Clinical Policy library and Mississippi provider pages and was unable to locate a Molina Clinical Policy specific to total shoulder arthroplasty (CPT 23472); the only related published policy I located addresses shoulder arthroscopy, a different procedure. Because I have not been given or been able to locate the actual criteria Molina applied to my request, I cannot and do not quote any Molina policy language in this letter regarding what "supports medical necessity" for this procedure — I am not aware of any such published Molina-specific language. I am formally requesting, as part of this appeal, that Molina identify by name, number, and edition/version the specific guideline (whether a Molina Clinical Policy, MCG Care Guideline, InterQual criteria, or other resource) that was used to review my request, and provide me a copy of that guideline, consistent with my appeal rights. If Molina supplies that document, I ask for the opportunity to respond to its specific criteria before a final decision is issued.

2. The clinical record supports medical necessity

In the absence of the plan's own stated criteria, I address the reason given — that "the imaging findings submitted do not support the medical necessity of the requested procedure" — using the clinical record already in Molina's possession:

- Imaging: Shoulder radiographs (true AP and axillary views) dated 2026-06-05 show complete loss of glenohumeral joint space with osteophytes, subchondral sclerosis, and a flattened glenoid. CT performed the same date confirms an intact rotator cuff. These findings document end-stage glenohumeral joint disease, which is the imaging basis for the requested arthroplasty. If Molina's clinical reviewer found this imaging insufficient, I ask that Molina explain specifically what additional imaging finding, view, or study was required and against what published standard, so that this can be addressed directly.

- Duration and severity of symptoms: I have had 24 months of progressive shoulder pain that is unrelieved by rest.

- Failed conservative treatment: I completed 12 weeks of supervised physical therapy (2026-04-27 to 2026-07-20, 16 visits) focused on range-of-motion and periscapular strengthening, as documented in my physical therapy discharge note; I used NSAIDs for 6 months with inadequate relief; and I received a corticosteroid injection on 2026-06-17 that gave only two weeks of partial relief.

- Functional impairment: I am unable to reach overhead, dress without help, or sleep on the affected side.

- Physical examination: My treating surgeon documented glenohumeral crepitus, active forward elevation limited to 90 degrees, and external rotation limited to 10 degrees, with cuff strength intact — consistent with the imaging findings of severe glenohumeral arthritis and an intact rotator cuff.

- No contraindications: I have no active infection, no untreated substance use, a BMI of 29, and I am a non-smoker.

Taken together, the imaging, exam findings, symptom duration, and documented failure of a full course of conservative management (physical therapy, medication, and injection) support the medical necessity of total shoulder arthroplasty. I ask that Molina's reviewing physician re-examine this complete record, including the enclosed documents, in light of this appeal.

3. Requested action

I request that Molina:
(a) reverse the denial and authorize CPT 23472 as requested by Dr. Okafor; or, in the alternative,
(b) identify the specific policy or clinical guideline applied, the specific criterion or criteria within it that Molina determined were not met, and what additional information would be needed to meet them, so that I may supplement the record accordingly.

I understand from Molina's published appeal information that "You or Your Authorized Representative may file a request for an internal review of an Adverse Determination within 180 days from receipt of the Adverse Determination," and I am submitting this appeal within that period. I also understand that if I am not satisfied with Molina's response to this internal appeal, I may request an external review through the Mississippi Insurance Department.

Enclosed with this letter:
- Physical therapy discharge note (2026-04-27 to 2026-07-20)
- Medication/injection records (NSAID trial; corticosteroid injection 2026-06-17)
- Shoulder radiograph report, 2026-06-05
- Shoulder CT report, 2026-06-05
- Office/exam notes documenting range-of-motion, strength, and functional limitations
- Letter of medical necessity from Dr. Okafor, MD
- [Any additional supporting records]

Please direct correspondence regarding this appeal to me at the address and phone number above, or to my authorized representative, [name/contact, if applicable]. I also request written confirmation of receipt of this appeal and the reference number under which it is being processed.

Thank you for your prompt attention to this matter.

Sincerely,

Riley Novak
